public_rationale: Read plainly, the claim says scaling was the main bet behind AI progress from about 2020 to 2025, and that it shaped research, investment and policy. The sources back this. Ilya Sutskever, OpenAI's former chief scientist and a key architect of scaling, calls 2020–2025 'the age of scaling'. He says companies preferred it as a low-risk way to invest. Epoch AI estimates that about two-thirds of language model progress over the past decade came from scale, with training compute growing 4-5x a year. The 2025 US AI Action Plan calls advanced compute 'essential to the AI era' and is built around compute and data-centre infrastructure. The claim holds under the plain reading. It is less certain under a strong reading, in which most people believed scaling alone would deliver AGI. No cited source measures that.
limitations: The outcome depends on reading 'scale is all you need' as scaling being the dominant strategy, not a universal belief that scaling alone gives AGI.
The Sutskever quotes come through a news write-up of a podcast.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: Scale-is-all-you-need has been the dominant view for five years, shaping AI research, investment and government policy.

statement.excerpt: It’s been the dominant view for the last half decade, shaping not only AI research, but investment and even government policy.
statement.document_title: “Scale Is All You Need” is dead

our_interpretation: Plain reading: from about late 2020 to late 2025, scaling up models (more compute, data and parameters) was the main strategy for AI progress. It drove frontier research, large AI investment, and government AI policy.

I do not require proof that most researchers believed scaling alone would reach general intelligence. The sentence is about scaling being the dominant view and shaping research, investment and policy, not about any one person's stated belief.
Government policy is tested with US federal AI policy documents from the period.
criteria.support_condition: Credible sources show that scaling was the main strategy behind frontier AI progress in 2020–2025, that investment followed it, and that government policy centred on compute and infrastructure.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Credible sources show that scaling was a minor or contested strategy in that period, or that investment and policy were organised around other approaches.

evidence.excerpt: Now, from 2020 to 2025, it was the age of scaling—maybe plus or minus, let’s add error bars to those years—because people say, ‘This is amazing. You’ve got to scale more. Keep scaling.’ The one word: scaling.”
evidence.explanation: A central figure in the scaling approach describes 2020–2025 as the 'age of scaling'. This matches Marcus's 'last half decade' of dominance in research.

evidence.excerpt: Companies love this because it gives you a very low-risk way of investing your resources. It’s much harder to invest your resources in research.
evidence.explanation: Sutskever says scaling shaped how companies invested their resources. This backs the investment part of the claim.

evidence.excerpt: we estimate that about two-thirds of the improvements in performance in language models in the last decade have been due to increases in model scale.
evidence.explanation: An independent research group finds that scaling was the main source of language model progress. The same report finds training compute grew 4-5x a year.
